title: Slim Lamar and Ray Bonitas becoming a bass player
summary: Hirsch recalls the band that went to Jackson, Mississippi with a Conn sales manager, where he moved from piano to drums and Ray Bonitas was made a bass player.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: What other bands did you work with over on the Gulf Coast?
Gulf Coast? Uh-huh. Gulf Coast. That was about the only one. The one with the...

Well, that was the first band that was over there. I know it was a long time ago. And, uh... It was... I don't know who the hell was the leader of it. I think it was Ellis Straticus. I'm not sure. But then later, I found a name of... Johnny, uh... He was a sales manager for CG Khan. He said, well, we went up to Jackson, Mississippi. Slim Lamar. Slim Lamar was his name. He was a sales manager for the head of the Khan agency down here. He was a man by the name of Teet. I don't know if you remember that.
No. No, I don't know that.

He was a sales... He was a... He was a manager. Slim was a sales manager. He had a brother by the name of Ewell Lamar. Who was a piano player. Not a good one, but... He was a piano player. And, uh... After we left... In Biloxi... Ray Bonitas was playing drums. And we went up to... Play up in Jackson, Mississippi. Well, Slim was with... Sales manager for Khan. And what they were trying to do... They were trying to build bands up in Mississippi. School bands, huh? And, uh... Ray Bonitas... When Slim's brother Ewell... Needed a job, he came with the band. Well, they took me off a... Off a piano... And put me on drums... And they said, what we gonna do with Ray's? Make him a bass player. So we went and bought a bass from Ray Magnum... For Ray Bonitas. And that's how he became a bass player. And he became a good one.
That's when Ray became a bass player.
